thread:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: spike detected — api-gateway-us-east-1 (502/504) error rate > 10% over 5m. Paging SRE on-call. Metrics: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/ingress
alice.nguyen: seeing the same. 502s concentrated on /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings. Any customer reports?
support-bot: Support tool: 2 high-priority customers filed timeouts, ticket IDs #2029, #2030. Noted increased retry rate from clients.
kevin.cho: I'm oncall. jumping in — pulling logs now. Can someone post the most recent rollout history for ingress? :eyes:
alice.nguyen: last deploy to api-gateway cluster was 2026-03-16 22:44 UTC, image tag service/api-gw:2026-03-16-rc4
kevin.cho: looking at edge proxy logs, lots of upstream reset and 502 from mux layer. snippet:
```
2026-03-17T00:02:11Z edge-proxy[proc]: upstream response: 502, connection reset
2026-03-17T00:02:12Z edge-proxy[proc]: upstream id=eu-mux-12 latency=12ms status=502
2026-03-17T00:02:14Z edge-proxy[proc]: io timeout to 10.0.45.78:443
```
kevin.cho: TL;DR: edge -> mux failing intermittently. I'm ssh-ing to a healthy node to run tcpdump. Anyone see recent changes to header/size or timeouts in the deploy config?
tara.ops: I can flip traffic to fallback mux pool (us-west) if we want to reduce customer impact. Prep the router toggle, @kevin.cho?
mike: Support update: customers experiencing 10-20s timeouts, some retries succeed. We're notifying affected accounts on the temp status page.
kevin.cho: ok hold — trying quick mitigation: enable 503-to-502-suppress? no... I'll roll edge-proxy back one revision for affected nodes. Running: `kubectl rollout undo deploy/edge-proxy -n ingress --to-revision=3`
oncall-bot: Rollback requested by kevin.cho — starting rollout undo on ingress/edge-proxy
alice.nguyen: I'm throttling client retries at the gateway layer to reduce cascading load (`rate_limit: 50rps` for suspect routes)
kevin.cho: after rollback, initial nodes show error rate dropping from 18% -> 8% in 2 minutes. Still watching.
jessica.sre: monitoring: error rate trending down across regions; some eu-east muxes still noisy. Suggest circuit-breaker on mux pool with 30s cooldown.
tara.ops: traffic shift started to fallback mux pool (us-west) — reduced traffic to us-east by ~40% via router toggle. :white_check_mark:
kevin.cho: found a bad config in last deploy: `x-forwarded-max-size` decreased default causing upstream to drop large payloads. Rolling back that config permanently in the next patch.
mike: Can someone capture a post-rollback flamegraph or relevant traces for the postmortem? I'll create the doc and link.
alice.nguyen: capturing traces now, saving traces to https://internal.redwood/doc/incident/5998881234/traces
oncall-bot: Incident update: customer-impacting = true -> partial, mitigation in progress. Pager muted for oncall rotation (kevin.cho) until next update.
kevin.cho: error rate back to baseline ~1.2% after 10m, majority of requests healthy. Handing off to tara.ops for night watch and follow-up postmortem.
tara.ops: taking handoff. I'll keep traffic shifted for 30m and then gradually move back with health checks. Opening follow-up doc: https://internal.redwood/doc/incident/5998881234/postmortem
mike: thanks team — support will send a customer update and we’ll coordinate the postmortem later today. :pray:
jessica.sre: leaving a note to include rollout gating and pre-deploy load tests in the action items.
kevin.cho: thx all. If error flares again ping me directly. Closing the live triage thread, moving to follow-up channel.
support-bot: Tickets #2029 and #2030 updated with status: mitigated, ETA for full RCA posted in postmortem doc.
